themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 14 this week—a 96% jump from the 7.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting an emerging environmental or building systems failure affecting multiple residential units across Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 14 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (96% spike, z-score: 3.9)
Spike is statistically significant and classified as high severity
No clear external cause identified in available data; suggests acute building or environmental trigger
reporting_angles: Door-knock survey of affected buildings to identify common complaints (mold, chemical odors, HVAC failures)
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if air monitoring or industrial sources are involved
Check if spike correlates with recent construction, heating system shutdowns, or hazmat incidents in the district

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping and Sanitation Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 13 last week—a 259% increase from the 3.6 weekly baseline—while sanitation worker complaints simultaneously spiked 500% (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 average), pointing to a potential sanitation service failure or staffing crisis.
evidence: 13 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 3.6 weekly average (259% spike, z-score: 3.75)
3 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 3.54)
Concurrent community board budget request for 'more frequent litter basket collection' (standing request, unsolved for years)
Long-running baseline demand: 1,322 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (3rd highest category)
reporting_angles: Obtain Department of Sanitation staffing logs for the district—check for absences, route cancellations, or vehicle breakdowns in the past 2-3 weeks
Interview residents on affected blocks to determine if sweeping stopped, frequency declined, or worker conduct issues occurred
Cross-check 311 complaint locations to identify geographic pattern (single neighborhood or district-wide)

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints exploded to 1,500% above baseline two weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average), the single largest statistical spike in the dataset, suggesting a sudden dumping event or bike-share malfunction affecting neighborhood accessibility.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,500% spike, z-score: 8.66—highest z-score in dataset)
Spike is concentrated and time-bound (single week), suggesting acute event rather than trend
Classified as high severity by statistical model
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike operations to determine if there was a service disruption, maintenance issue, or fleet repositioning in the district 2-3 weeks ago
Geomap the 311 complaints to find if bikes are concentrated in a single neighborhood or transit hub
Interview sanitation or Parks Enforcement to understand removal timeline and whether residents face citation or barriers to cleanup

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 20 complaints three weeks ago—a 233% increase from the 6.0 weekly average—reflecting accelerating pedestrian infrastructure failure across the district during spring weather transition.
evidence: 20 sidewalk condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.0 weekly average (233% spike, z-score: 6.6)
Related spikes in curb condition (3 complaints last week vs. 1.1 average, 167% increase, z-score: 3.13)
Street condition complaints rank #9 in 90-day volume (677 total), indicating sustained baseline infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Request Department of Transportation complaint maps and repair backlog data—determine if spike exceeds typical spring repair season
Interview community board members about whether sidewalk reconstruction funding is available or pending
Walk affected blocks to photograph conditions and document hazards (tripping risks, ADA barriers)

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Concerns Near Recent Fatal Fire
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 4 incidents three weeks ago—a 256% spike from the 1.1 weekly average—appearing shortly after the fatal Inwood apartment fire (May 10–12) that drew scrutiny to building code enforcement and landlord violations across the district.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (256% spike, z-score: 3.1)
Spike occurred in immediate aftermath of high-profile fatal fire (May 10–12) and landlord violation reporting

Recent Gothamist article ('Resident flicked cigarette that caused fatal Inwood fire') and THE CITY article ('Landlords in Fatal Fire Racked Up More Than 1,000 Violations') indicate heightened scrutiny of building safety and maintenance
reporting_angles: Determine whether food poisoning complaints cluster near the fire site or are district-wide—food inspection failures may indicate broader building system negligence
Cross-reference food poisoning 311 complaints with Department of Health inspection records for those addresses—check violation patterns and landlord histories
Interview Department of Health about whether fire incident prompted retaliation visits or accelerated inspections in the district
